summary: @ornikar/jest-config preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated in-tarball payload
details: package.json declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`, which runs automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs is obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style identifiers (`_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`,...) and, at install time, downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/...zip`, extracts it, chmod +x's the binary, and invokes it via `execFileSync` against a sibling file `math_init.js` — a ~727 KB obfuscated bundle shipped in the tarball (leading numeric constant array plus a `WV8StW` shift-based array rotator). The package presents itself as a Jest configuration preset, which has no legitimate need to fetch an alternate language runtime or execute a large opaque bundle at install time. Using Bun to execute the payload also bypasses Node-oriented tooling and static review. The combination of unrelated-runtime fetch, obfuscated install-time launcher, and obfuscated bundled payload executed under that runtime matches the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
